business_description:
Merlin Entertainments is the world's third-largest location-based family entertainment company by visitors, operating 131 attractions across 22 countries as at FY2025 year-end, welcoming 60.5 million guests and generating £1,999m of revenue in FY2025 (source: 9fin key financial table, LTM/Annual series, cited https://9fin.com/company/Merlin%20Entertainments/financials; Q4 2025 earnings transcript, 24-Mar-2026, https://9fin.com/transcripts/b3a20b0a-50a2-434f-804c-9cb25200715d). The estate is organised around three brand groups: LEGOLAND Parks (11 resorts including the newly opened Legoland Shanghai; c.43% of LTM Sep-2024 revenue), Gateway/Midway Attractions (branded, predominantly indoor city-centre and mall-based attractions including Madame Tussauds, SEA LIFE, the Dungeons, and the London Eye; c.36%), and Resort Theme Parks (six outdoor parks including Alton Towers, Thorpe Park, Chessington, Warwick Castle and Gardaland; c.21%) (source: 9fin Credit QuickTake, 27-Jan-2025, https://9fin.com/news/1ebca1ec-45f4-4026-b167-75048b5f8bc9). Merlin holds the exclusive worldwide LEGOLAND brand licence from KIRKBI (the Lego founding family's holding company) until at least 2075, paying a low single-digit percentage of revenue royalty (source: same Credit QuickTake).

Revenue is generated predominantly from visitor admissions and in-attraction commercial spend (c.82% of revenue), with accommodation (c.14%) and other income (c.4%) making up the balance (source: 9fin Credit QuickTake, 27-Jan-2025). Geographically the group reported under four regions through FY2025 (North America, UK, Continental Europe, Asia Pacific); from FY2026 Europe and Asia Pacific were combined into a single 'International' segment for reporting purposes (source: Q1 2026 earnings review, 29-May-2026, https://9fin.com/news/59bc9a23-02c6-4009-80b4-be183b0e6ffd).

Corporate history: Merlin was taken private in October 2019 by a consortium led by KIRKBI and Blackstone (co-investors since 2005 under a prior management buy-out), joined by Canada Pension Plan Investment Board (CPPIB/CPP Investments) as a new investor in the 2019 deal, at an enterprise value of c.£5.9bn (c.12x the then £494m underlying EBITDA), funded with £3.3bn of new debt that took leverage from c.4x (2018) to c.7.5x post-acquisition per S&P (source: 9fin analysis 'Merlin faces short window to deal with SUNs', 3-Nov-2025, https://9fin.com/news/d204d377-5c3d-48df-8286-84faaff6b63d). Current ownership: KIRKBI 47.49%, Blackstone 31.99%, CPP Investments 15.5% (source: 9fin Credit QuickTake, 27-Jan-2025); the balance (c.5%) is not itemised in sources reviewed — not available - further diligence required (likely source: Annual Report shareholder register note). In September 2025 Merlin sold its 29 Lego/Legoland Discovery Centres to sister company The Lego Group (also KIRKBI-owned) for c.£200-216m, completing 27-Feb-2026 (source: 9fin news and FY25 earnings review, 25-Mar-2026, https://9fin.com/news/968e1b7e-cbb6-4631-b93c-a9e5bc909bc0). FY2025 accounts also recognised a £262m impairment on the Madame Tussauds brand, reflecting a conservative valuation reset given weaker North American/Asian trading (source: Q4 2025 transcript). Most recently, Merlin confirmed on 10-Sep-2026 a £657m senior secured term loan (led by Monarch and GoldenTree, with Oaktree Capital also participating) to refinance its £627-630m of senior unsecured notes due Nov-2027, secured on a portfolio of previously unencumbered UK assets — see pf_credit_metrics and uk_asset_context below for full detail (source: 9fin news, 10-Sep-2026 and 17-Sep-2026).

summary_financials.fcf_basis: Calculated from EBITDA build using 9fin's reported cash flow statement line items (cash tax paid, working capital movement, capex, cash interest paid, finance lease capital repayments). Merlin has been structurally levered-FCF-negative in every period shown, consistent with 9fin's own analysis ('we expect Merlin to continue to burn over £100m levered FCF in each of the next two years', 9fin analysis 3-Nov-2025).

pf_credit_metrics.context: On 10-Sep-2026 Merlin confirmed a new £657m senior secured term loan ($396m + €418m tranches, led by Monarch and GoldenTree Asset Management, with Oaktree Capital also participating) to refinance its $410m 6.625% and €370m 4.500% senior unsecured notes due Nov-2027 (c.£627-630m equivalent). The facility is priced at 650bps over the relevant benchmark (SOFR/EURIBOR), matures in 6 years with a springing maturity that pulls the date forward to before 2030 if the SUNs are not otherwise refinanced, and is secured pari passu alongside the existing senior secured debt. Transaction expected to close by end-2026; as at the last 9fin cap table (30-Jun-2026) the transaction had not yet closed and is NOT reflected in the reported capital structure below — all PF figures are pre-close estimates. Sources: 9fin news 10-Sep-2026 (https://9fin.com/news/b9ef800a-31a3-4e7d-9597-8492eac34786), 9fin analysis 10-Sep-2026 (https://9fin.com/news/7bbf2ed4-3a88-48dd-aaf8-3752b643a9d3), 9fin news 17-Sep-2026 (https://9fin.com/news/d2468584-df61-4bbb-99c2-19d9a2fc68de).

This £535m figure is a 9fin analyst estimate, not a company-disclosed number.

This is a 9fin analyst estimate, not a disclosed coupon — flagged accordingly.
cash_interest_pre_vs_pf.estimated_incremental_annual_interest: c.£30m per year (9fin back-of-envelope estimate: c.£65m new facility interest vs c.£35m coupon on notes refinanced)

This is CMCK's own calculation combining a reported current-period actual with a 9fin analyst estimate for the incremental piece; the underlying new-facility rate is undisclosed by the company, so treat this PF figure as indicative only.

pf_interest_cover.current_reported: 1.5x (Adj. EBITDA £568m / finance costs £380m per 9fin income statement, matching 9fin's own reported 'Interest coverage (IFRS16)' of 1.5x LTM)
pf_interest_cover.pf_estimate: c.1.4x-1.5x (£568m Adj. EBITDA / c.£379-410m estimated PF cash interest or finance costs, depending on whether the £30m incremental interest is added to the cash-paid base of £349m or the P&L finance-cost base of £380m). Both bases point to modest further compression from the current 1.5x. This is a CMCK calculation built on the 9fin coupon estimate above, not a disclosed figure — treat as indicative only, further diligence required for the actual new-facility terms once the transaction documentation is filed.

pf_leverage.current_total_net_leverage_post_IFRS16: 9.5x (£5,416m net debt / £568m Adj. EBITDA, LTM 27-Jun-2026, per 9fin cap table)
pf_leverage.current_secured_net_leverage: 5.5x (£3,140m net secured debt / £568m Adj. EBITDA, per 9fin cap table)
pf_leverage.pf_total_net_leverage_estimate: c.9.5x-9.7x, broadly unchanged from the current 9.5x. The £657m new secured facility is intended as a like-for-like refinancing of the c.£627-630m of SUNs being taken out, so gross/net debt should move only modestly (by the size of any OID, fees, or incremental new money, none of which is disclosed). On 9fin's own 'cleaner' £535m EBITDA basis (ex-LDC), this would imply c.10.1x-10.3x — consistent with 9fin's own commentary that leverage is 'estimated now at around 10x' post-transaction.
pf_leverage.pf_secured_net_leverage_estimate: c.6.6x-6.8x (CMCK calculation: current £3,140m net secured debt + c.£657m new secured facility ≈ £3,797m, over £568m Adj. EBITDA), up materially from the current 5.5x reported secured leverage. This priming effect (unsecured debt being replaced by new secured debt ranking alongside the existing SSNs/TLBs) is the reason 9fin's 17-Sep-2026 article reports the 2030s, 2031s and 2032s falling 2-5 points on the announcement even as the SUNs rallied toward par — the market's read that relative recoveries for the existing secured stack are diluted. This PF secured leverage estimate is a CMCK calculation from disclosed inputs, not a company or agency-confirmed figure; further diligence recommended once the transaction closes and a post-close cap table is available.
pf_leverage.caveat: None of the PF leverage or PF interest cover figures above are company-disclosed pro forma figures. They are CMCK calculations built from the last reported (pre-close) cap table plus the deal terms and 9fin analyst estimates set out in the sources cited. The transaction was not yet closed as at the last available 9fin cap table date (30-Jun-2026) or as at today (28-Sep-2026); expected close is by end-2026.

uk_real_estate_and_new_collateral.new_secured_facility_collateral: The £657m new secured term loan (confirmed 10-Sep-2026) is secured against a portfolio of previously unencumbered UK assets specifically identified as the London Eye, SEA LIFE London, Shrek's Adventure! London, and the UK Dungeons. The company stated it retains full ownership and management of these assets. Source: 9fin news 10-Sep-2026 (https://9fin.com/news/b9ef800a-31a3-4e7d-9597-8492eac34786) and 17-Sep-2026 (https://9fin.com/news/d2468584-df61-4bbb-99c2-19d9a2fc68de).
uk_real_estate_and_new_collateral.important_correction_vs_freehold_assumpt: 9fin's own June-2026 pre-deal analysis of Merlin's unencumbered-asset options states that these specific Gateway attractions — Madame Tussauds, the Dungeons, Discovery Centres and the London Eye — sit on LEASED sites, not freehold land (source: 'How might Merlin tackle upcoming SUN maturities?', 19-Jun-2026, https://9fin.com/news/22e48f42-cd8c-4d57-8958-51a0e50501d9). This means the new collateral pool is very unlikely to be freehold real estate in the way a mortgage security package would be; it is more likely security over the operating entities, leasehold interests, brand/IP value and cash flows of these specific London attractions. This has not been independently confirmed from primary deal documentation (not yet filed/available on 9fin at the time of this review) — not available - further diligence required (likely source: the new facility's security/collateral agreement once filed, or a 9fin legal analysis of the transaction once documentation is public).
uk_real_estate_and_new_collateral.freehold_vs_leased_estate_generally: Per the same 9fin analysis (19-Jun-2026), Merlin's owned freehold estate is concentrated in LEGOLAND Parks internationally (with several leased exceptions), Gardaland, Chessington, and a handful of smaller Gateway sites. By contrast, Alton Towers, Thorpe Park, Heide Park and Warwick Castle (all Resort Theme Parks) are LEASED from LondonMetric, and the Legoland Windsor Hotel (though not necessarily the park itself, which is not separately itemised in sources reviewed) is also leased. This is a material correction to the common assumption that Merlin's flagship UK theme parks are freehold-owned: per 9fin's sourced review of the OM's property schedule, most are not. Legoland Windsor Park's freehold/leasehold status specifically was not itemised in the sources reviewed — not available - further diligence required.
uk_real_estate_and_new_collateral.unencumbered_asset_estimate: 9fin's analysis estimated c.£0.7bn of unencumbered fixed assets sitting at non-guarantor subsidiary level (as of Q1 2026, applying a 69%/31% guarantor/non-guarantor asset split to £2.3bn of group PP&E) that could in principle support further structurally senior debt — relevant context for what capacity may remain after this £657m facility. Source: 9fin analysis, 19-Jun-2026.
